title: Exponential Hardness of Off-Policy Evaluation under History-Dependent Logging
why_read: A theoretical result showing exponential sample complexity for off-policy evaluation under history-dependent logging is a niche but rigorous contribution to reinforcement learning theory.
analysis: The paper constructs explicit POMDP examples showing that even with good state and belief coverage, off-policy evaluation can require an exponential number of logged episodes when the logging policy depends on history. This resolves an open question about whether certain coverage conditions guarantee tractable evaluation, showing they do not in this setting. It's a solid theoretical contribution mainly of interest to RL theorists working on off-policy evaluation guarantees, with limited direct applicability for practitioners.
